_notes: Scores: 4 bytes on 4-byte centres from 0x021109E4. Stride 8 yields 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF.
current_player and current_ball were resolved by the joint pair test, not by reading bytes.
Independent 1->2->3 detection could not do it here: 0x00037315 topped the sweep at 680 hits
against a next-best of 130 and is not a counter at all -- 0x00037314 holds a rising 32-bit
little-endian value and 0x37315 is its second byte, reading 1, 2, 3 as it crosses 256, 512 and
768. Searching a static exit dump for an adjacent (player=4, ball=3) pair gave 40 candidates.
Requiring the two bytes to move together -- the player wrapping to 1 in the same sample the ball
steps up -- returned exactly one hit for the whole game, and it is one of those 40.
Free Play derived by aligning this game's adjustment array against a game where it was measured
(32/35 agreement), which places it at index 33, 0x02102110. The value there reads 1 on a cabinet
in free play and its check byte validates. Machine adjustments are 8-byte records from
0x02102008: a 32-bit little-endian value, then a byte holding 0xFF minus the sum of the value's
four bytes. All 88 records here satisfy that. Writing this field requires updating its check
byte, or the game discards the change on reload.
The check byte is declared with an explicit checksum address. Without one, a checksum8
record means the checksum occupies the tail of start..end, which is not this layout: here
the summed bytes and the check byte are separate fields of one record.
